outcome: Several narrow special cases of Beilinson's (and the closely related Beilinson-Bloch / Beilinson-Bloch-Kato) conjectures were settled in 2025: for certain K3 surfaces with an involution (Banerjee), for certain products of curves with powers of CM elliptic curves over function fields (Broe), for certain abelian surfaces conditional on BSD (Banerjee), and conditional progress on polarized motives (Peng). The general conjectures remain wide open; no AI involvement was found in any of this work.
summary: Wikipedia's bullet is unqualified 'Beilinson's conjectures' — the general statements relating orders of vanishing/special values of L-functions to ranks of motivic cohomology and regulators. These remain open in general; the article's own lead ('known to be true only in special cases') has not changed and has no post-2024 references. Since the 26 January 2024 freeze, four preprints have settled genuine special cases: (1) Kalyan Banerjee, arXiv:2502.09380 (submitted 2025-02-13, revised 2026-03-05), proves Beilinson's conjecture unconditionally for certain K3 surfaces over the algebraic closure of ℚ admitting an involution whose quotient is P² branched along a sextic; (2) Matt Broe, arXiv:2505.00696 (submitted 2025-05-01), gives a criterion for the Beilinson-Bloch conjecture over global function fields and deduces it for products of curves with powers of CM elliptic curves, via a proof of the Tate conjecture in that setting; (3) Kalyan Banerjee, arXiv:2509.24645 (submitted 2025-09-29), proves the Bloch-Beilinson conjecture for certain abelian surfaces over ℚ conditional on BSD holding for those surfaces; (4) Hao Peng, arXiv:2509.18615 (submitted 2025-09-24), makes conditional/partial progress on the Beilinson-Bloch-Kato conjecture for polarized motives. Each of these is a genuine restriction of the general conjecture (a specific variety type, or a specific base field) rather than a different conjecture altogether, so I classify this as 'partial' rather than 'open' with no_change_found — the territory covered by the general conjecture has been reduced, if only slightly and in some cases conditionally. None of the four papers mentions any AI or machine-learning tool in their abstracts, introductions, or (where checked) metadata; all are traditional single- or dual-author pure mathematics papers using classical techniques (Chow groups, regulators, Tate conjecture arguments, Iwasawa theory). A broad search for any AI system credited with progress on Beilinson's conjectures, the Beilinson-Bloch conjecture, or the Beilinson-Bloch-Kato conjecture (including checking Wikipedia's own 'List of mathematical discoveries by artificial intelligence') turned up nothing. The dated event I anchor status to is the earliest of the four preprints (Banerjee, Feb 2025); the other three are described above rather than given separate records, per the instructions to describe multiple events in summary.
competing_reading: One could argue these four results are all instances of derivative/related conjectures (Beilinson-Bloch, Beilinson-Bloch-Kato) rather than 'Beilinson's conjectures' as Wikipedia's bullet names them, and that the bullet — being unqualified and pointing at the general L-function/regulator framework — is not moved at all by results confined to Chow groups and algebraic cycles on specific surfaces. Under that stricter reading the status would be 'open' with no_change_found true, since no result changes what a careful person would write about the general, unqualified conjecture. I lean toward 'partial' because Beilinson-Bloch and Beilinson-Bloch-Kato are standard extensions/refinements of the same conjectural framework attributed to Beilinson and treated by experts (e.g. Nekovář, Deninger-Scholl) as part of the same conjectural family that the Wikipedia bullet is gesturing at, and each paper explicitly proves cases of a 'Beilinson' or 'Bloch-Beilinson' conjecture rather than a conjecture with different hypotheses.
what_would_settle_it: A clear statement from an expert survey or the Wikipedia article itself on whether Beilinson-Bloch / Beilinson-Bloch-Kato are considered the same conjecture family as the bullet's 'Beilinson's conjectures' or a genuinely distinct (if related) conjecture; absent that, the classification rests on my own reading of the literature's naming conventions.

judgement.doubts: Partial rests on unreviewed special cases of the Bloch-Beilinson/Beilinson-Bloch branch of the conjectural family; if the bullet is read narrowly as Beilinson's L-value/regulator conjectures only, these are variants and the status would be open. The two conditional results (reductions to BSD or other unproven hypotheses) cannot set status. Broe is the more solid of the two surviving cases; both are confirmed, no AI, so the codes don't change.
